reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) strongly supports the baseline instability and the nature of the degradation (coarsening, Al-Zr precipitation), but provides no data on yttrium additions, their segregation behaviour, or their effect on microstructural stability in this alloy system. The key premises involving yttrium are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: AlMo0.5NbTa0.5TiZr has an initial nanoscale B2+bcc microstructure that is unstable at 800–1200 °C
Instability involves coarsening and intragranular Al-Zr-rich intermetallic precipitation
Yttrium additions can segregate to grain boundaries and form interfacial phases
Grain-boundary phases can pin boundaries and retard coarsening/precipitation
Yttrium at ~1–2 at% can be distributed without forming excessive brittle intermetallics
